title: The Last Crown
premise: Noor Nystrom, the guild's invisible cartographer, discovers the fallen border wards were anchored to a covenant sealed in dragon-fire centuries ago—and that the guild itself helped break it. To restore it, Noor must cross three dying realms with a disgraced ward-keeper and a dragon's last heir, trading secrets they've guarded all their life for allies they never meant to need. At the Ember Threshold, Noor learns the covenant demands a crown-bearer's willing sacrifice; they offer their own name instead, unmaking their place in every ledger and map. The wards rise again, the stars return, and Noor—nameless but remembered by the found family who refuses to forget—begins drawing a new map with no borders at all.
about_author: Lior Underhill is the pseudonym of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who keep the world running quietly, and who are finally forced to stop.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. While balancing the guild's impossible ledgers, Noor notices entries vanishing—the same night the wards collapse and the stars gutter dark. When guildmaster Vess orders the truth buried, Noor instead copies the forbidden covenant maps and flees with ward-keeper Sef, who was blamed for the collapse. Emotional beat: fear transforming into defiant choice; the invisible made visible.

chapters.title: A Cartography of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor and Sef POV. Crossing the drowned realm of Miravelle, they find the first anchor-stone and a dying dragon heir, Ashk, who reveals the guild traded the covenant's fire for profit generations ago. Noor's maps literally burn where lies were drawn. Emotional beat: the ache of learning your family's foundation was a betrayal, and choosing your companions anyway.

chapters.title: The Ember Threshold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the threshold, the covenant's ghost-judge demands a crown-bearer's willing death to reforge the wards—and names Noor, whose hidden royal lineage the ledgers always knew. Sef and Ashk refuse to let them die alone, standing witness. Emotional beat: climax of love against duty, as Noor rewrites the terms with a cartographer's precision, offering their name instead of their life.

chapters.title: Unmapped
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, then Noor's. The wards blaze back to life; the stars return over a realm that no longer remembers Noor's name—except Sef and Ashk, who carve it into the restored anchor-stone. The guild scatters, and the three begin mapping a borderless world together. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the price of survival paid, and found family refusing to let sacrifice mean erasure.
